function: Excluded, above_phy: the deep Q-learning agent learns UAV trajectory and IoT device scheduling (p. 6); RIS phase shifts come from a non-learned 2D-DFT codebook search (p. 7).
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Excluded as above_phy. p. 6: "Action space: The agent controls two aspects:" the UAV move (left, right, forward, backward, stop) and "IoT devices wireless scheduling, where the agent selects a" subset of devices; the reward counts served devices (p. 6). Sub-problem 2, the RIS phase shifts, is not learned: p. 7: "codebook, and the received signal power is used to find the best" configuration of a 2D-DFT codebook. Figs. 3-6 (pp. 9-10) compare the DRL plus codebook scheme with a non-optimised trajectory, a stationary UAV and non-optimised (random) RIS phases; no RIS, power, bandwidth or beam control is learned. Borderline: the authors call the scheduling 'radio resource allocation' (pp. 3, 6), but the agent only selects which devices upload in each slot, so I read it as scheduling plus UAV trajectory, both listed above the physical layer. If the reviewer reads the scheduling as aerial-link resource allocation, the work would pass this check and fall in area 6 (RIS-assisted UAV, ris = 1). The exclusion also holds under the literal no_learning wording (no learned component sets a physical-layer quantity); I chose above_phy because a learned component exists and acts above that layer.
